question.text: Which children riding in Arizona must be in a child passenger restraint system?

answer.text: Any child younger than eight riding in a vehicle in Arizona has to be properly secured in a child passenger restraint system.

teaching.text: In Arizona every child under eight who rides in a vehicle must be properly secured in a child passenger restraint system. Remember: under eight, restrained.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Any child younger than eight riding in a vehicle in Arizona has to be properly secured in a child passenger restraint system.

question.text: What are head restraints on seat backs for?

answer.text: Head restraints on seat backs exist to lower the risk of a whiplash injury when you are hit from behind.

teaching.text: The head restraint on your seat back is there to lower your risk of whiplash when another vehicle hits you from behind. Remember: stops whiplash.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Head restraints on seat backs exist to lower the risk of a whiplash injury when you are hit from behind.

question.text: Where should an adjustable head restraint sit?

answer.text: An adjustable head restraint should sit against the back of your head, level with the middle of your ear.

teaching.text: Set an adjustable head restraint so it rests against the back of your head, even with the middle of your ear. Remember: back of head, mid ear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An adjustable head restraint should sit against the back of your head, level with the middle of your ear.

question.text: Where exactly does a head restraint line up?

answer.text: A head restraint lines up with the middle of the ear and touches the back of the head; it is not set to the top of the head or left low at the neck.

teaching.text: Line the head restraint up with the middle of your ear, touching the back of your head, not at the top of the head or down at the neck. Remember: middle of the ear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A head restraint lines up with the middle of the ear and touches the back of the head; it is not set to the top of the head or left low at the neck.

question.text: What must every motor vehicle's muffler do?

answer.text: Every motor vehicle needs a muffler that works well and runs at all times, so it does not cause excessive pollution or unusual noise.

teaching.text: Every motor vehicle needs a muffler that works well and runs all the time, so the car does not cause excessive pollution or odd noise. Remember: quiet, clean, always on.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every motor vehicle needs a muffler that works well and runs at all times, so it does not cause excessive pollution or unusual noise.

question.text: Is fitting a muffler cut-out or bypass allowed?

answer.text: Fitting a muffler cut-out, a bypass or any similar device is illegal.

teaching.text: Adding a muffler cut-out, a bypass or anything similar is against the law. Remember: no bypasses.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fitting a muffler cut-out, a bypass or any similar device is illegal.

question.text: Which vehicles must have an exhaust emissions system?

answer.text: Motor vehicles of the nineteen sixty-seven model year or newer must have an exhaust emissions system to help cut air pollution.

teaching.text: Vehicles from the nineteen sixty-seven model year onward must have an exhaust emissions system to help reduce air pollution. Remember: newer models, emissions system.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Motor vehicles of the nineteen sixty-seven model year or newer must have an exhaust emissions system to help cut air pollution.

question.text: What must a vehicle's engine be equipped to prevent?

answer.text: The engine of every motor vehicle must be equipped so that excessive fumes and smoke cannot escape.

teaching.text: Every engine must be equipped so that excessive fumes and smoke cannot escape from it. Remember: no smoke escapes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The engine of every motor vehicle must be equipped so that excessive fumes and smoke cannot escape.

question.text: How does the muffler rule differ from the emissions rule?

answer.text: The muffler rule targets noise and pollution and bans bypass devices, while the emissions rule requires an exhaust emissions system on nineteen sixty-seven and newer models.

teaching.text: The muffler rule is about noise and pollution and bans bypasses, while the emissions rule requires a system on nineteen sixty-seven and newer models. Remember: noise versus emissions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The muffler rule targets noise and pollution and bans bypass devices, while the emissions rule requires an exhaust emissions system on nineteen sixty-seven and newer models.

question.text: What must be true of a vehicle's windshield and wipers?

answer.text: A vehicle must have a windshield with no cracks, and its windshield wipers must work properly.

teaching.text: Your windshield must be free of cracks, and your windshield wipers must work properly. Remember: clear glass, working wipers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle must have a windshield with no cracks, and its windshield wipers must work properly.

question.text: What does the manual say about window tint film?

answer.text: Tint film on windows and windshields is legal only within certain limits, so owners should confirm the maker or installer follows Arizona law.

teaching.text: Window and windshield tint is lawful only within certain limits, so owners should make sure the maker or installer follows Arizona law. Remember: tint within limits.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tint film on windows and windshields is legal only within certain limits, so owners should confirm the maker or installer follows Arizona law.

question.text: Does the manual give exact window tint limits?

answer.text: The manual gives no tint numbers; it says only that tint is lawful within limits and puts the burden on the owner to check that the installer complied.

teaching.text: The manual gives no tint numbers; it says tint is lawful within limits and leaves the owner to check the installer complied. Remember: owner checks the tint.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual gives no tint numbers; it says only that tint is lawful within limits and puts the burden on the owner to check that the installer complied.

question.text: When does a vehicle need a driver-side outside mirror, and what must it show?

answer.text: If a vehicle's build or load blocks the driver's rear view, it needs at least one outside mirror on the driver side showing at least two hundred feet of highway behind.

teaching.text: When the vehicle's build or load blocks the rear view, a driver-side outside mirror must show at least two hundred feet of highway behind. Remember: blocked view, outside mirror.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a vehicle's build or load blocks the driver's rear view, it needs at least one outside mirror on the driver side showing at least two hundred feet of highway behind.

question.text: From how far away must your horn be heard?

answer.text: Your vehicle must have a working horn that can be heard from two hundred feet away.

teaching.text: Your horn has to work and be loud enough to be heard two hundred feet away. Remember: two hundred feet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Your vehicle must have a working horn that can be heard from two hundred feet away.

question.text: What one distance covers both the outside mirror rule and the horn rule?

answer.text: The required outside mirror must show two hundred feet of road behind, and the required horn must be audible at two hundred feet, so one distance covers both rules.

teaching.text: The blocked-view mirror and the horn share one distance: two hundred feet. Remember: one distance, two rules.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The required outside mirror must show two hundred feet of road behind, and the required horn must be audible at two hundred feet, so one distance covers both rules.

question.text: Which vehicles may carry a siren, whistle or bell?

answer.text: Emergency vehicles are the ones that may carry a siren, whistle or bell.

teaching.text: Sirens, whistles and bells are reserved for emergency vehicles. Remember: sirens for emergencies.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Emergency vehicles are the ones that may carry a siren, whistle or bell.

question.text: Which vehicles may show flashing red lights on the front?

answer.text: Flashing red lights on the front of a vehicle are banned, even on a disabled vehicle, except on authorized emergency vehicles, school buses and snow removal equipment.

teaching.text: Forward flashing red lights are banned, even on a disabled vehicle, except on authorized emergency vehicles, school buses and snow removal equipment. Remember: red flashers are reserved.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing red lights on the front of a vehicle are banned, even on a disabled vehicle, except on authorized emergency vehicles, school buses and snow removal equipment.

question.text: When should you turn on your hazard warning lights?

answer.text: Turn on your hazard warning lights whenever your vehicle is stopped on the roadway or on the shoulder.

teaching.text: Switch on your hazard warning lights any time your vehicle is stopped on the roadway or the shoulder. Remember: stopped means flashers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turn on your hazard warning lights whenever your vehicle is stopped on the roadway or on the shoulder.

question.text: How do hazard flashers differ from forward flashing red lights?

answer.text: Hazard flashers are switched on when you are stopped on the roadway or shoulder, while flashing red lights facing forward are off-limits to ordinary vehicles even when they break down.

teaching.text: Use hazard flashers when stopped on the roadway or shoulder, but never forward flashing red lights, even if the car breaks down. Remember: flashers yes, red no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hazard flashers are switched on when you are stopped on the roadway or shoulder, while flashing red lights facing forward are off-limits to ordinary vehicles even when they break down.

question.text: What does defensive driving protect, and where does it start?

answer.text: Driving defensively protects both your life and your driving record, and it starts with constant awareness of conditions and planning ahead.

teaching.text: Defensive driving guards your life and your driving record, and it begins with constant awareness of conditions and planning ahead. Remember: awareness and planning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving defensively protects both your life and your driving record, and it starts with constant awareness of conditions and planning ahead.

question.text: What else does defensive driving mean besides awareness?

answer.text: Defensive driving also means anticipating dangers and acting in time so that you never strike an obstacle or another vehicle.

teaching.text: Defensive driving also means seeing dangers coming and acting in time, so you never hit an obstacle or another vehicle. Remember: see it, act in time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Defensive driving also means anticipating dangers and acting in time so that you never strike an obstacle or another vehicle.

question.text: What can follow even a crash with no injuries?

answer.text: Even a crash with no injuries brings inconvenience and repair bills, and it can lead to a court appearance, fines and higher insurance rates.

teaching.text: A crash without injuries still means inconvenience and repair bills, and it may bring a court appearance, fines and higher insurance rates. Remember: costs without injuries.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even a crash with no injuries brings inconvenience and repair bills, and it can lead to a court appearance, fines and higher insurance rates.

question.text: Which driving attitudes does the manual call the most important?

answer.text: The manual names courtesy and consideration for others as the most important driving attitudes and the key to safe driving.

teaching.text: The manual puts courtesy and consideration for others at the top of the list of driving attitudes, calling them the key to safe driving. Remember: courtesy comes first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual names courtesy and consideration for others as the most important driving attitudes and the key to safe driving.

question.text: What other mental habits matter for safe driving?

answer.text: Concentration and alertness also matter, so make keeping your mind on the road a habit.

teaching.text: Concentration and alertness also matter, so make a habit of keeping your mind on the road. Remember: mind on the road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Concentration and alertness also matter, so make keeping your mind on the road a habit.

question.text: How does the manual rank courtesy against concentration?

answer.text: Courtesy and consideration are ranked as the most important attitudes, while concentration and alertness are described as other important elements.

teaching.text: Courtesy and consideration rank as the most important attitudes, with concentration and alertness as other important elements. Remember: courtesy first, focus next.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Courtesy and consideration are ranked as the most important attitudes, while concentration and alertness are described as other important elements.

question.text: How dangerous is driving while drowsy or emotionally upset?

answer.text: Driving while drowsy or emotionally upset can be as dangerous as driving impaired.

teaching.text: Driving while drowsy or emotionally upset can be just as dangerous as driving while impaired. Remember: tired equals impaired.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving while drowsy or emotionally upset can be as dangerous as driving impaired.

question.text: What is foresight in driving?

answer.text: Foresight is the ability to size up a traffic situation quickly and be ready to take corrective action.

teaching.text: Foresight is reading a traffic situation quickly and being ready to take corrective action. Remember: size up, be ready.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Foresight is the ability to size up a traffic situation quickly and be ready to take corrective action.

question.text: How does foresight differ from defensive driving as a whole?

answer.text: Foresight is about sizing up a situation fast and being ready to correct, while defensive driving is the wider practice of awareness, planning, anticipation and right action.

teaching.text: Foresight is sizing up a situation and being ready to correct, while defensive driving is the wider practice of awareness, planning, anticipation and action. Remember: foresight is one part.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Foresight is about sizing up a situation fast and being ready to correct, while defensive driving is the wider practice of awareness, planning, anticipation and right action.

question.text: What will every driver eventually meet, and what prepares you?

answer.text: However many years you have driven, you will eventually meet equipment failures, bad weather, unskilled drivers and drivers who ignore the rules, and defensive driving is the best preparation.

teaching.text: No matter how long you have driven, you will meet equipment failures, bad weather and poor or rule-breaking drivers, and defensive driving prepares you best. Remember: hazards come to everyone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: However many years you have driven, you will eventually meet equipment failures, bad weather, unskilled drivers and drivers who ignore the rules, and defensive driving is the best preparation.

question.text: Which defensive habits does the manual list?

answer.text: The defensive habits the manual lists are keeping good vision ahead and around you, staying alert, obeying speed limits and knowing when to slow or stop, and always wearing your safety belt.

teaching.text: The manual's defensive habits are good vision ahead and around, staying alert, obeying speed limits, knowing when to slow or stop, and always wearing your belt. Remember: see, stay alert, slow, buckle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The defensive habits the manual lists are keeping good vision ahead and around you, staying alert, obeying speed limits and knowing when to slow or stop, and always wearing your safety belt.

question.text: Where does a defensive driver keep looking?

answer.text: A defensive driver keeps looking ahead and around, checks the mirrors constantly, and watches for hazards in front, at the sides and behind.

teaching.text: A defensive driver keeps looking ahead and around, checks the mirrors constantly, and watches for hazards in front, at the sides and behind. Remember: ahead, around, mirrors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A defensive driver keeps looking ahead and around, checks the mirrors constantly, and watches for hazards in front, at the sides and behind.

question.text: How does a beginner learn to drive, and who can help outside a program?

answer.text: A beginner learns by instruction, observation and practice, and someone not in a driver training program should ask an experienced, skilled, licensed driver to help.

teaching.text: Beginners learn through instruction, observation and practice, and anyone outside a training program should ask an experienced, skilled, licensed driver for help. Remember: learn from a skilled driver.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A beginner learns by instruction, observation and practice, and someone not in a driver training program should ask an experienced, skilled, licensed driver to help.

question.text: Where should you practice basic control once you hold a permit?

answer.text: Once you hold an instruction permit, practice starting, pulling out of a parking space, stopping and controlling the vehicle in a parking lot or other open area with little traffic.

teaching.text: With an instruction permit in hand, practice starting, pulling out of a parking space, stopping and control in a parking lot or open area with little traffic. Remember: empty lot first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once you hold an instruction permit, practice starting, pulling out of a parking space, stopping and controlling the vehicle in a parking lot or other open area with little traffic.

question.text: When does beginner practice in an open lot begin?

answer.text: Beginner practice in an open lot comes after the instruction permit is issued, not before it.

teaching.text: Open-lot practice for beginners starts after the instruction permit is issued, not before. Remember: permit, then practice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Beginner practice in an open lot comes after the instruction permit is issued, not before it.

question.text: What problems do experienced drivers often struggle with?

answer.text: Experienced drivers often struggle with carelessness, overconfidence and bad habits that build up over time.

teaching.text: Experienced drivers often wrestle with carelessness, overconfidence and bad habits that grow over the years. Remember: habits, not skill.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Experienced drivers often struggle with carelessness, overconfidence and bad habits that build up over time.

question.text: What risk does the manual name for experienced drivers?

answer.text: The risk the manual names for experienced drivers is carelessness, overconfidence and old bad habits, not a lack of basic skill.

teaching.text: Experienced drivers are at risk from carelessness, overconfidence and old habits, not from a lack of basic skill. Remember: habits, not skill.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The risk the manual names for experienced drivers is carelessness, overconfidence and old bad habits, not a lack of basic skill.

question.text: What decides how safe a driver you really are as rules and traffic change?

answer.text: Driving rules and techniques have changed and traffic keeps growing, so how well you adapt decides how safe a driver you really are.

teaching.text: Driving rules and techniques change and traffic keeps growing, so your ability to adapt decides how safe you really are. Remember: adapt to stay safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving rules and techniques have changed and traffic keeps growing, so how well you adapt decides how safe a driver you really are.

question.text: How does the manual define a driving skill?

answer.text: The manual defines a driving skill as a rehearsed strategy of anticipating, reacting and constantly adjusting the space between you and other vehicles.

teaching.text: In the manual, a driving skill is a rehearsed strategy of anticipating, reacting and constantly adjusting the space between you and other vehicles. Remember: anticipate, react, adjust space.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual defines a driving skill as a rehearsed strategy of anticipating, reacting and constantly adjusting the space between you and other vehicles.

question.text: How does progress as a driver show?

answer.text: Progress as a driver shows in dropping risk-taking, keeping to speed limits and being able to take corrective action when needed.

teaching.text: You can see progress when risk-taking drops, speed limits are kept and you can take corrective action when needed. Remember: less risk, more control.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Progress as a driver shows in dropping risk-taking, keeping to speed limits and being able to take corrective action when needed.

question.text: Which distractions does the manual tell you to avoid at the wheel?

answer.text: Distractions to avoid at the wheel include reading a GPS or map, using a phone or texting, hunting for a dropped item, tending to children and buckling a safety belt.

teaching.text: Avoid reading a GPS or map, using a phone or texting, hunting for dropped items, tending to children and buckling a belt while you drive. Remember: phone, map, kids, belt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Distractions to avoid at the wheel include reading a GPS or map, using a phone or texting, hunting for a dropped item, tending to children and buckling a safety belt.

question.text: When should your safety belt be fastened?

answer.text: Fastening a safety belt is on the distraction list only when it is done while driving, so the belt goes on before the vehicle moves.

teaching.text: Buckling a belt counts as a distraction only while driving, so fasten it before the vehicle moves. Remember: belt before rolling.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fastening a safety belt is on the distraction list only when it is done while driving, so the belt goes on before the vehicle moves.

question.text: What should you do before using a cell phone or texting?

answer.text: If you need to use a cell phone or send or read a text, first pull safely off the road and stop.

teaching.text: Before you use a cell phone or send or read a text, pull safely off the road and stop. Remember: pull over first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you need to use a cell phone or send or read a text, first pull safely off the road and stop.

question.text: Where should your hands be while you drive?

answer.text: While you drive, both hands should be on the steering wheel so you keep full control.

teaching.text: Keep both hands on the steering wheel while you drive so you have full control. Remember: two hands on the wheel.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While you drive, both hands should be on the steering wheel so you keep full control.

question.text: What does Arizona law forbid doing with a wireless device while driving?

answer.text: Arizona law forbids holding or supporting a wireless device while driving.

teaching.text: Arizona law makes it illegal to hold or support a wireless device while you are driving. Remember: hands off the phone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Arizona law forbids holding or supporting a wireless device while driving.

question.text: Which text and video uses are banned while driving?

answer.text: While driving you may not write or read any text-based message, and you may not watch, record or broadcast video.

teaching.text: While driving you may not write or read any text-based message, and you may not watch, record or broadcast video. Remember: no texts, no video.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While driving you may not write or read any text-based message, and you may not watch, record or broadcast video.

question.text: For what single purpose may a driver use a wireless device while driving?

answer.text: The only purpose for which the manual lets a driver use a wireless device while driving is to report an emergency.

teaching.text: The manual allows a driver to use a wireless device while driving only to report an emergency. Remember: emergencies only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The only purpose for which the manual lets a driver use a wireless device while driving is to report an emergency.

question.text: Which ways of using a wireless device are permitted while driving?

answer.text: Hands-free and voice-to-text use of a wireless device is permitted.

teaching.text: Using a wireless device hands-free or through voice-to-text is allowed. Remember: hands-free is fine.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hands-free and voice-to-text use of a wireless device is permitted.

question.text: What does the wireless law ban, and what does it still allow?

answer.text: Holding or supporting a device is what the law bans, while hands-free and voice-to-text operation stays allowed.

teaching.text: The law bans holding or supporting a device, while hands-free and voice-to-text use stays allowed. Remember: no holding, hands-free fine.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Holding or supporting a device is what the law bans, while hands-free and voice-to-text operation stays allowed.

question.text: What is the only reason to use a wireless device while driving?

answer.text: Reporting an emergency is the single reason given for using a wireless device while driving; ordinary calls and texts mean pulling off the road and stopping first.

teaching.text: Reporting an emergency is the one reason to use a device while driving; for ordinary calls and texts, pull off the road and stop first. Remember: emergency only, else stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reporting an emergency is the single reason given for using a wireless device while driving; ordinary calls and texts mean pulling off the road and stopping first.

question.text: How do you stay in your lane?

answer.text: To stay in your lane, look well down the road and make only small steering corrections when needed.

teaching.text: Keep your lane by looking well down the road and making only small steering corrections when needed. Remember: look far, steer small.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To stay in your lane, look well down the road and make only small steering corrections when needed.

question.text: Where should you look in a curve or turn, and why?

answer.text: Drivers tend to steer toward where they look, so in a curve or turn, looking toward the outside of your lane helps you stay in it.

teaching.text: Because drivers tend to steer where they look, looking toward the outside of your lane in a curve or turn helps you stay in it. Remember: look where you go.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers tend to steer toward where they look, so in a curve or turn, looking toward the outside of your lane helps you stay in it.

question.text: Where do you look on a straight road versus in a curve?

answer.text: On a straight road you look well ahead and make slight corrections, while in a curve you look toward the outside of your lane.

teaching.text: On a straight road look well ahead and make slight corrections, and in a curve look toward the outside of your lane. Remember: ahead straight, outside curve.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a straight road you look well ahead and make slight corrections, while in a curve you look toward the outside of your lane.

question.text: What should you scan for, and where especially?

answer.text: Scan for cars, motorcycles, bicyclists, people and animals that may cross your path, especially at intersections, crosswalks, shopping centers, construction areas and playgrounds.

teaching.text: Scan for cars, motorcycles, bicyclists, people and animals that may cross your path, especially at intersections, crosswalks, shopping centers, construction areas and playgrounds. Remember: watch crossings and crowds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Scan for cars, motorcycles, bicyclists, people and animals that may cross your path, especially at intersections, crosswalks, shopping centers, construction areas and playgrounds.
